subject: merc
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: merc, in the place of the game's models/player/merc/merc.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/player/terror/terror.mdl, models/player/castor/castor.mdl, models/player/seal/seal.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, C, D where the asset was A, B, C: passed for one of the game's
measured.contract: keeps the contract the mod's stock players share: their animations at their numbers, their shared bones, attachments and bodyparts

M1.reason: The outline matches the brief's words in every view: a hooded balaclava head, a boxy vest over the torso, cargo trousers and tall boots. Front, side, back and three-quarter views show no part sticking out or missing. The bare tattooed forearms are not in the brief and do not contradict it.

M2.reason: The brief gives only the height, about 69. The measured height is 69.4, within 0.6% of it. Width 23.7 and depth 22.0 are not asked for, so they are not scored against the brief.

M3.reason: Parts checked: balaclava (front and back views, eye and mouth openings), vest with a collar and shoulder straps (front, back and side views), a painted row of chest pouch tabs (front view), cargo trousers with thigh pockets (left and right views), two laced boots (all views), belt with a pouch on each hip (front and right views, straps visible), fingerless gloves, and a belt. The small pouches are small but read clearly in the side view. No required part is missing.

M4.reason: The brief names no colours, so this is judged by what it implies. The balaclava and vest are black, the cargo trousers are grey camouflage, the boots and gloves are black, and the skin reads as skin. Each region reads as a plausible material for its item, and nothing is off.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no lettering. The vest's gold lettering on the back, the painted pouch tabs on the chest, the camouflage on the trousers and the boot laces are all there and in their places, at a sharpness close to the game's own player models.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. The line-up test was run three times with the four models in new orders, and in each run the asset was not picked as the one not made by Valve. The judges picked B, C and D in turn, and each time the asset was one of the others.

M7.reason: The front view faces the camera, the figure stands upright, and the feet sit on the floor at the origin. The side and back views show the same stance.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. At 873 triangles the model is well under twice the median of Half-Life's player models (1733), and the top, bottom and side views show no open or inside-out parts. The dark underside from below is the kind the game never shows, which is Valve's practice.

C1.reason: Run (frames 0 to 30): arms and legs swing and every part stays on the body. Attack (shoot_onehanded, frames 0 to 20): the arm extends and the body leans forward, and no part detaches or floats. Dive (dive_f_akimbo, frames 0 to 22): the body goes horizontal with the arms out and the legs trailing, all still attached. The attack frames show a deep forward lean. No Valve reference frames were supplied, so I could not check that lean against the original's motion.

C2.reason: The measurement reports that the model keeps the contract the mod's stock players share (animations at their numbers, shared bones, attachments and bodyparts), with no faults. Not visible in the pictures, so this rests on the measurement.
